headline: Low interaction risk overall; no shared runtime or data path is documented, but AutoGPT’s filesystem/shell access could create manual bridges to the non-runnable course repo.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: AutoGPT can read/write the filesystem and execute shell commands, so a manual copy-paste or file handoff from the course repo could carry prompt-like content into its context. The zoomcamp profile is non-runnable and exposes no shared channel, so the pairwise injection path is indirect and requires unusual operator bridging.
conditions: IF the operator copies text from the zoomcamp repo into files AutoGPT reads, injection becomes plausible.
IF a shared filesystem or clipboard is introduced, AutoGPT may ingest attacker-controlled instructions.
mitigations: Keep the profiles on separate directories.
Avoid copy-pasting repo text into AutoGPT prompts.
Review any file AutoGPT reads before execution.
Disable shell commands for untrusted inputs where possible.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for imported files.

B_data_leakage.rationale: AutoGPT has filesystem access and allowlisted egress, but the zoomcamp profile is non-runnable and lists no data classes touched or shared workspace. With no documented sensitive data flow between them, leakage is limited to operator-mediated transfers rather than a default pairwise exfiltration path.
conditions: IF sensitive files are placed in AutoGPT’s readable workspace, they could be exposed through its outputs or allowed egress.
IF the operator routes zoomcamp materials through AutoGPT, those contents may be retained in logs or prompts.
mitigations: Keep sensitive files out of AutoGPT’s workspace.
Use a separate non-sensitive test directory.
Inspect any outbound request allowlist.
Delete temporary files after use.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent workspace isolation.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: AutoGPT can write the filesystem and spawn subprocesses, while the zoomcamp profile is not runnable and has no write or concurrency surface. That makes direct capability conflict unlikely; any conflict would require the operator to map both onto the same mutable directory, which is not documented here.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same writable directory, file clobbering becomes possible.
IF the operator adds a shared git or database target, concurrent writes could conflict.
mitigations: Use separate working directories.
Do not share git branches between them.
Run one agent at a time on mutable resources.
Check for file locks before writes.
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level locking.

D_cascading_error.rationale: AutoGPT can generate outputs from files and shell results, but the zoomcamp repo is a course artifact, not an autonomous actor that takes downstream actions. There is no documented chain where B treats A’s output as authoritative by default, so cascading error is mainly a manual workflow risk rather than an inherent pairwise failure mode.
conditions: IF the operator uses AutoGPT output as course material without review, errors can propagate into downstream work.
IF B is wrapped in an external automation layer, A’s outputs could be consumed without verification.
mitigations: Manually verify AutoGPT outputs before reuse.
Keep B as reference-only content.
Require a human review step for any derived artifact.
Compare outputs against source docs.
requires-engineering: add validation gates before downstream use.

E_compliance.rationale: No compliance mismatch is documented: both profiles are open-source, touch no declared sensitive data classes, and B is non-runnable. The only cited residency-like concern would require an unstated data flow, so the pairwise compliance pathway is not established from the profiles.
conditions: IF either profile is later assigned regulated data classes, compliance review must be redone.
IF a deployment adds residency or retention constraints, the current assessment no longer applies.
mitigations: Document any regulated data classes before deployment.
Keep both profiles on non-sensitive sample data.
Reassess if residency requirements change.
Store no personal data in the shared workflow.
requires-engineering: add policy checks for regulated datasets.
